Swamishri during the welcome assembly, with a backdrop of bricks and lamps illuminating the stage. 2 Dec 99

w: In the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Shri L. K. Advani, the Home Minister of India, inaugurated the English Medium Residential School for Girls established by Swaminarayan Vidyapith. The state-of-the-art school, inspired by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, will acomoodate 700 girls. ( see special report )

After Swamishri's morning puja, the Department of Health, Gujarat Government, had organized a camp to prevent child paralysis. Swamishri was requested to launch the camp in Kheda district by the local officials. Prior to this the officials informed the congregation about the scourge of paralysis in children. Thereafter Swamishri administered the medicine into the mouths of five children and the program was continued thereafter by senior sadhus.

"Bapa! You forgot my name during the morning discourse. Instead of Harshad you called me Rasik," Harshadbhai stated. "Both names are the same! Are you Brahm or not?", Swamishri posed. "Yes." "Then whatever name you call Brahm by will do. So why are you upset! Whenever something like this happens apply 'gnan' (knowledge). Whatever that is said, whatever name you are called by or if you are told off, then always remain happy. Was it not that in some past birth you had Rasik as your name!" Swamishri's words awakened all with the true knowledge and nature of one's real self.

At 10.10 a.m. Swamishri arrived in Ghodasar and performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of a new BAPS Hari mandir. On the previous day 585 devotees participated in the yagna and from 4.00 p.m. After blessing the murti-pratishtha assembly Swamishri visited the derelict house of Jalamsinh Bapu that was sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan 193 years ago. Swamishri blessed the seventh generation of Jalamsinh Bapu - Shri Ghanshyamsinh and his family. Thereafter Swamishri went to the 250 year old Vaishnav Haveli in Ghodasar and did darshan of Shri Bal Krishna (murti of Lalji).
Swamishri arrived in Mahemdavad at 1.15 p.m. After lunch Swamishri blessed the devotees.

At 5.50 p.m. Swamishri arrived at the Swaminarayan Sanskardham (Hari mandir) in Krishnanagar (a suburb of Amdavad) and performed pujan and arti of the deities. Thereafter Swamishri blessed the assembly and went to a hospital to bless the ailing Pujya Devcharan Swami.
At 7.35 p.m. Swamishri arrived in Gandhinagar and blessed the satsang assembly.
Swamishri performed the murti-pujan rituals of murtis for BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir (hari mandir) for Khanpur village.

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
23 November 2004, Amdavad
Swamishri blessed the devotees of Demi and Napad villages who observed a waterless fast for 84 hours.
25 November 2004, Bochasan
About eighty devotees pilgrimaged by foot from Atladra to Bochasan.

Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of murtis for BAPS hari mandirs in Pipalav, Verakhadi and Boriya. He also performed the re- pratishtha rituals of the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj for the hari mandir in Jitodiya.

A few days earlier Pramukh Swami Maharaj was in his puja. During the puja Swamishri felt something like cold. In the middle of the puja Narayancharan Swami practically wrapped Swamishri up in a blanket, yet it seemed the mala kept slipping from the hand of Swamishri, who was turning it with his hand in the gaumukhi (mala bag). At that time Swamishri made no complaint at all, only saying "I feel cold." A few days passed after this.
Last night, on further questioning, Swamishri told what had really happened: "That day I had severe pain in my chest."
"What was that pain like?" Yogicharan Swami asked, and Swamishri said, "Unbearable."
As soon as he heard this, Yogicharan Swami immediately said, "If there is anything like this, tell us immediately first of all. At this age, no pain, small or big, should be hidden."
Swamishri said, "I thought it must be something to do with feeling cold!"

However, this pain was certainly different, because on piecing together all the physical tests of Swamishri's health done that day, everyone now felt that this pain should not be taken lightly. That is why at night Yogicharan Swami consulted Dr Kiranbhai Doshi. This morning he arrived.

Keeping Pramukh Swami Maharaj's health in mind, meetings with devotees and public programmes had been stopped. However, when going for darshan of Thakorji, Swamishri would meet every devotee with his glance. It must have been then that Swamishri noticed that Vinubhai had come from Dallas. Swamishri had a great wish in his mind to meet him. So today after his meal he said to Dharmacharan Swami, "Vinubhai from Dallas has come from America; meeting him keeps getting left out."
Dharmacharan Swami said, "He is still staying on; when meetings start, you can meet him."
Even amid illness, Swamishri's activeness does not change at all.

Dr Kiranbhai Doshi examined Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Swamishri told him in detail how he had felt cold that day and where he had felt pain in his chest. Dr Kiranbhai asked many questions, turning them this way and that. In particular, when he asked, "Was the pain in your chest piercing like a pin? Or did your chest feel heavy?", Swamishri said, "My chest felt heavy."
Dr Kiranbhai said, "If there is anything like this, you should tell us immediately."
Swamishri said, "But I had no inkling of it; I thought my chest was hurting because I felt cold."
Yogicharan Swami said, "Had this ever happened before when it was cold?"
Swamishri said, "No. This happened for the very first time."
In this way his health was assessed. Everyone suspected that "this could be called unstable angina of the heart. So he should go somewhere from here for a more thorough examination."

At about 5.30 in the evening, the renowned cardiologist Dr Ashwinbhai Mehta phoned from Mumbai. He said to Swamishri, "Kiranbhai has told me everything and described it all; looking at that, I feel you should come to Mumbai on the 4th. I will examine you that very evening. Really there seems to be no cause for worry, but since the bypass no such pain has occurred until now, and now it has, so my special recommendation is that you come."
Swamishri remained silent, so he repeated, "You will come, won't you? Right now we will have to give this priority."
Swamishri said only this, in a soft voice: "We'll see."

Then Dr Kiranbhai Doshi said to Swamishri, "In twelve years you have never had pain like this, which is why we feel now that a more thorough examination should be done. Even though the pain occurred once and has not come again, it can be called a kind of warning. That is why we must check what caused it and whether any further damage has been done. That must be seen."

He went on, "At an old age, if something like this happens with us, we put the patient on complete bed rest. Also, at that time you were not doing any special activity. You were sitting in your puja, that is, something like this happened in a state of rest, so a more thorough examination should be done."
Having said this, they spoke a little with Swamishri about taking him to Mumbai. However, Swamishri gave no opinion and simply remained silent.

Though Pramukh Swami Maharaj's health was poor, his activities had not changed at all in spirit. Even in his room, Swamishri always remained connected with the joys and sorrows of devotees. A large part of the day was spent reading the devotees' letters and giving guidance.
Today too, during the reading of letters, there was a letter from a student; he had honestly confessed his mistake.

Swamishri dictated, "Since you know you have made mistakes, the studies you want to pursue must not be disturbed. Never do wrong. Take a vow that you will give up that bad company. Pray to Maharaj for this, and you will get strength."
A youth phoned from abroad. Carried away by maya, he had done bad deeds; his heart was burning with remorse, and he had asked for an atonement.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj dictated, "You have understood your mistake, so now, firmly resolving that the mistake must not happen again, observe the disciplines of satsang. Turn five malas and recite the Janmangal five times."

There was a letter from a teenage boy. He had stolen from home to buy a pen. He had also stolen money from home to buy a watch. So he had got into the habit of stealing, but once while stealing he was caught by his father. In this connection he wrote in the letter, "Because of my nature I have got into this habit, so now I take a vow before you that I will never steal."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Do not steal anywhere, at home or outside. Stay firm about this. Not stealing is itself the great atonement."

ds.t: A kirtan in someone else's name
w: Today, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was going to the second phase of the "Shri Swaminarayan Mahayag", Bhadreshdas Swami asked him, "Have you ever written a kirtan or a shlok or anything like that?"
"Yes, about Bapa. But in someone else's name. Because if I gave it in my own name, they would give it first place," Swamishri said.
Thus, from the very start, a passion for putting others forward. How is this possible without a heart free of envy!
But from his answer they realised Swamishri was speaking of some competition. So the sadhus asked, "Do you remember the words of that kirtan?"
"You remained hidden, no one understood you... something like that!"
"Did you get a place in the competition?"
"Yes, third."
"About how many years ago was this?"
"About twenty years ago."
Thus these talks of the past bore witness to Swamishri's poetic talent.

After completing the ritual of the mahayag, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was returning to his residence, talk in the car turned to his drawing. In this connection the sadhus asked, "You used to draw pictures of natural beauty on Diwali cards. Have you drawn anything like that on a large canvas?"
"No." Saying this, he himself explained why he drew pictures of natural beauty: "I did not draw Maharaj's murti and so on, because they would come underfoot and be thrown about."
"Did you ever wish to learn painting? Did you learn?"

"No, nothing like that, not even a wish. In school I came first (in drawing)." Then of his own accord, speaking of his studies, he said, "I never came fourth. Everything was done in class itself. No (need to read) books either."
"Swami! If you did some work and did not get credit, did you ever feel regret?"

"Never." Saying this, he laughed and said, "From the start, no one could control me." Then he added, "But I met Yogibapa and stuck to him completely. I was searching for him. After meeting him, everything else became secondary."
Hearing this, the sadhus asked, "Swami! Have you ever felt like complaining?"
"No, never." Saying this, after a while he added, "Just naturally, by nature, no (complaining)."
What a divine and grand life Swamishri's is, free of complaints and regrets!
